architecture.summary: SO-06 adds the tenant provisioner of the control plane and the new owner render. The switch MCP_TENANTS_ENABLED is off by default: then the start reads no tenant setting and runs no loop. With it on, the start checks the Render key, workspace, registry credential, TENANT_IMAGE by digest, TENANT_PLAN_FREE, TENANT_NAME_PREFIX, GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY, and CONTROL_PLANE_INTERNAL_URL (the last two with the rules of the tenant role), needs the private hosted storage, and app starts one loop of tenants, which it stops before the SQL runtime closes. The loop claims one requested row at a time (a creating or deploying row first), names the Render service TENANT_NAME_PREFIX and the organization ID in lower case, searches by that name before it creates, and stops the row as failed for two services of the name. The create call makes an image-backed private service in oregon with a closed list of tenant variables (THERMUS_ROLE=tenant, TENANT_ORGANIZATION_ID, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, WORKOS_AUTHKIT_ISSUER, GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_INTERNAL_URL, OPERATION_CAPACITY=5 from the map free 5, team 10) and no secret. The loop reads the newest deploy every 5 s for at most 15 minutes and records live with http://<host of serviceDetails.url>:<open port> and the digest, or failed with the reason and one operator report; a deploying row after a resume also goes live. New external integration: the Render API, through the render adapter that implements the new public contract src/tenancy/tenants/tenant-platform.ts: reads and the delete have up to 3 attempts after a 429, a 5xx, or no answer; a create is sent one time in each attempt, at most 3 attempts, each after a search; the adapter counts the create window from the rate-limit headers; it refuses a write for a service that the registry does not own, and always for the production service srv-db8mnqg473hc739d529g. New edges: app -> render (runtime), render -> tenants (type), tenants -> system-logs (type); tenants never imports render. The registry gains provisioning statements (a claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and guarded state records) and no migration. The shared SQL runtime now gives each pg client an error listener, so a connection that the database ends while work holds the client fails that work instead of ending the process. app gains the Node builtin node:timers/promises for the waits of the loop; no package is added. The provisioner deletes nothing: SO-09 uses the delete of the adapter.
